title: Palindrome Partitioning II
description:
Given a string s, partition s such that every substring of the partition is a palindrome.

Return the minimum number of cuts needed for a palindrome partitioning of s.

A string that is already a palindrome requires zero cuts.

examples.explanation: The palindrome partitioning ["aa", "b"] could be produced using 1 cut.
A single character is already a palindrome, so no cuts are needed.
One cut splits "ab" into the palindromes "a" and "b".

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters only.
approach: Let cuts[k] be the minimum cuts needed for the prefix of length k, initialized to k-1 (the worst case of cutting every character), so cuts[0] = -1. Expand around every possible palindrome center (both odd-length single centers and even-length gaps). Each palindrome s[left..right] means the prefix ending at right+1 can be formed from the prefix ending at left plus one more piece, so cuts[right+1] = min(cuts[right+1], cuts[left] + 1). Expanding around centers enumerates all palindromic substrings without building a quadratic table. There are O(n^2) expansions, so time is O(n^2) and the cuts array uses O(n) space.
